label: late original-phase input of v/d/c/l/i after f/n/j earlier in the sequence
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98% of mass), at positions 3-8 (peak at orig_idx 5-6), never at t=0-1 and almost never on <DEL> or in the copy phase (the small copy-phase share is mostly at recall_idx 1-2 when f is output). The current input is mostly v, d, c, l, or i (about 75% of active steps), with weaker firing on 3, 2, x; it is near-silent on q, m, t, w. Rates are much higher when f, n, or j appeared earlier, especially as the first token (first_tok f/n ~4x lift), and when the input token is a first occurrence (in_first 1.6x vs 0.3x). Requiring an earlier f/n/j raises precision from 0.17 to 0.30 and puts more of the top quartile inside the predicate (75% coverage vs 38% in the bottom quartile), so the strongest activations (e.g. f f f j a b i d) are v/d/c/i after several f/n/j. Many v/d/c/l/i inputs after f/n/j still do not fire, so the neuron reads a distributed prefix state this token rule only approximates. Dev F1 0.39, mass recall 0.64; dropping the f/n/j condition gives mass recall 0.82 at precision 0.17.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: v, d, c, l, i, 3; least: e, z, j, f) and the first original token (most: f, n, j, g, z, p; least: c, i, v, d); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=8 & t=9, L=7 & t=8.
